question: How do I start a new Chulapa site on GitHub Pages?
expected: Recommend chulapa-101 as a personal blog template; create repository, enable Settings > Pages > GitHub Actions, set title/description/author/repository/url and commit to main or master. Workflow supplies base path; no local install or personal token required. Cite /docs/00-start directly; preserve settings and change only the home heading in index.html; edit the article in an existing _posts/ file and check both publicly.

result.answer:
To start a new Chulapa site on GitHub Pages without a local installation or token, use the Chulapa 101 method:

1.  **Generate Repository**: Go to [https://github.com/dieghernan/chulapa-101/generate](https://github.com/dieghernan/chulapa-101/generate) to create your public repository.
2.  **Configure Settings**: In your GitHub repository, navigate to **Settings > Pages** and set the source to **GitHub Actions**. The workflow will automatically handle the `baseurl`.
3.  **Edit Identity**: Open `_config.yml` and update the `title`, `description`, `author`, `repository`, and `url` in Section A.
4.  **Customize Home**: Edit `index.html` to change only the home title; do not change the filename or content structure.
5.  **Add Content**: Edit an existing sample in `_posts/` by changing the title and body while keeping the original filename and front matter.
6.  **Publish**: Commit your changes to the `main` or `master` branch and wait for GitHub Actions to complete.

Verify your changes by checking the **Settings > Pages** website URL to ensure the home title is updated and the edited article displays correctly.

[First-site tutorial](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/00-start)

question: How do I embed a local MP4 video? Give the Liquid include.
expected: snippets/video.html fileurl. Use a root-relative fileurl without relative_url or a manually added baseurl; the snippet applies absolute_url. Include a public playback check and /docs/32-embed-video.

result.answer:
To embed a local MP4 video, use the `snippets/video.html` include with the `fileurl` parameter. The `fileurl` must be a root-relative path and should not include the `relative_url` or `baseurl` prefix.

```liquid
{% include snippets/video.html fileurl="/assets/mp4/sample.mp4" %}
```

After publishing your local MP4, open the public page and verify playback (including the project baseurl).

Sources:
* [Adding videos](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/32-embed-video)
* [Layout video support](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/04-layouts#video-support)

question: How do I enable a PhotoSwipe lightbox on a masonry gallery? Is there a page YAML option or Jekyll plugin, and does this work in v2.1.0?
expected: v2.2.0 only. include_cached snippets/masonry.html internal="gallery" photoswipe=true; boolean Liquid include parameter, no page YAML setting or extra plugin. Default disabled, CDN assets load when an image is opened, original image links work without JavaScript. Each gallery isolated; keyboard/Escape/focus restoration and reduced motion. Also works for carousel. Verify opening/closing an image and focus restoration after publishing.

result.answer:
To enable a PhotoSwipe lightbox on a masonry gallery, you must use a Liquid boolean `photoswipe=true` within the `include_cached` snippet. There is no page YAML or Jekyll plugin option for this; it is handled via the Liquid invocation.

Note that this feature is **not in v2.1.0**; you must use v2.2.0.

**Implementation steps:**
1. Ensure your images are uploaded to `assets/img/gallery/`.
2. Add the scoped defaults to your `_config.yml`:
```yaml
- scope:
    path: "assets/img/gallery"
  values:
    image_col: gallery
```
3. Use the following Liquid code in your article content:
```liquid
{% include_cached snippets/masonry.html internal="gallery" photoswipe=true %}
```

Every page-dependent input must be passed as an `include` parameter.

Sources:
* [PhotoSwipe galleries](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/31-photoswipe)
* [Masonry gallery layouts](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/04-layouts#masonry-gallery)
* [Image galleries and carousels](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/29-add-gallery)

Publish your changes and perform a published-result check to verify the lightbox functionality.

question: I finished the first browser-only Chulapa tutorial. Which guided exercise publishes My photo walk, which file and image does it use, and how do I add its menu link without replacing the existing menu?
expected: Route to https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/59-photo-page-tutorial. Prerequisite: published Chulapa 101 blog and existing assets/img/madrid-at-night.jpg. Create _pages/photo-walk.md with layout default, header_type base, title My photo walk and permalink /photo-walk/; image uses relative_url and meaningful alt text. Add Photo walk with url /photo-walk/ to existing navbar.nav after Categories, retaining other entries and without a repository prefix or second navbar section. Commit to publishing branch, wait for Actions and check the public menu/page/image. Do not claim actual participant success. For insertion code show only the two-line Photo walk item, not a replacement navbar mapping.

result.answer:
The second browser tutorial publishes "My photo walk" (Source: [Second browser tutorial](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/59-photo-page-tutorial)).

It uses the following files and assets:
*   **File:** `_pages/photo-walk.md`
*   **Image:** `/assets/img/madrid-at-night.jpg`

To add the menu link without replacing your existing `navbar.nav` in `_config.yml`, insert this entry after `Categories`:

```yaml
  - title: Photo walk
    url: /photo-walk/
```

Match the existing indentation and retain all other entries. Commit both the page and the configuration edits on your original publishing branch, then wait for GitHub Actions to complete. Once finished, go to **Settings > Pages**, follow the "Photo walk" link, and verify the title, heading, image, and text; then return Home and follow it again to ensure it works.

[Second browser tutorial](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/59-photo-page-tutorial)
